title: Everything is numbers
debrief: A computer stores everything as numbers made of bits: letters, colours, pictures and sounds. The coding rule is public, which is why data works across devices. Encryption is something else: it locks data with a key.

items.text: The smallest piece of information is {0}. It has only two values: {1}.
items.why: A bit is a zero or a one. Everything else is made of bits.

items.text: Eight bits make {0}. It can hold {1} different values.
items.why: Each extra bit doubles the number of values: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 256.

items.text: In a computer the letter A is stored as the number {0}. The character table is known to {1}.
items.why: In the character table capital A is number 65. The table is public, so texts work on different computers too.

items.text: You write the colour of a pixel with three numbers: how much {0} it contains.
items.why: Each pixel has three numbers from 0 to 255. A photo from a phone has millions of them.

items.text: A picture of 8 × 8 pixels has {0} pixels. At 16 × 16 there are {1}.
items.why: Twice as many across and down is four times as many numbers, and so a file four times as big.

items.text: Coding is a {0} rule for writing data as numbers. Encryption locks data {1}.

options: with a key only someone has

items.why: Anyone can open a PNG or an MP3, because the rule is public. Only someone with the key can open an encrypted message.
